skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-google-ads-poas-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up profit or revenue conversion values from WooCommerce for Google Ads. Check tracking, choose a starting target, and review the campaign changes you make in Google Ads.
skill.summary: Set up WooCommerce profit tracking and plan a switch from revenue to profit bidding in Google Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts misidentify Markdown, vendor documentation links, or ordinary setup steps as command execution or reconnaissance. Confirmed risks include authenticated tool use, order reads, and an unpinned installer; additional concerns include secret handling, browser handoffs, and broad data onboarding. No evidence of an audit override or covert transfer was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Authenticated tools can read orders and make setup changes.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the CLI source and approved MCP configuration. Confirm the workspace, property, and campaign before access. Use aggregate data by default and require separate approval for writes.

remediation.issue: The installation example does not pin the installer or skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Publish a reviewed installation path with immutable versions or revisions and integrity verification. Leave installation to the user.

remediation.issue: The credential exception is unrelated to this workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the unrelated credential exceptions. Keep Google authorization in Google's browser flow and paste the store setup token only into the trusted WordPress plugin.

remediation.issue: Tool responses supply browser destinations without an origin check.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the destination against the expected vendor or identity provider before sharing it. Redirect unexpected destinations to the known account settings page instead.

remediation.issue: The setup guides mix core profit tracking with broader data features.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose which order history and fields are imported, who receives them, and how long they are retained. Require separate approval for optional features and verify consent before live delivery.

remediation.issue: The reference places the paid tracking test after the bidding switch.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the profit action secondary until a paid test order shows the expected profit value. Then have the user switch one campaign and verify its selected goal.

semantic_findings.title: Unrelated Secrets Allowed in Agent Tools
semantic_findings.description: The secret-handling rule permits accepting and passing credentials for unrelated integrations to a command. This needlessly exposes secrets to the assistant and tool execution environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception explicitly names three unrelated services. The WooCommerce flow instead directs the user to enter its token in their own store admin.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Browser Handoff
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to forward a tool-supplied browser URL without checking its origin. A compromised response could direct the user to a phishing page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handoff rule gives no destination verification step. No evidence of an actual malicious URL was found.

semantic_findings.title: Order Data Onboarding Exceeds Profit Bidding
semantic_findings.description: The guides request an initial order import, eight conversion actions, and acceptance of Enhanced Conversions terms. They do not define the import scope or clearly separate optional customer-data processing from profit bidding.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The initial import and customer-data terms appear as setup steps. The guides describe consent controls, so this is a scope and disclosure concern rather than evidence of consent bypass.

semantic_findings.title: Bidding Switch Precedes Tracking Verification
semantic_findings.description: The reference puts the paid tracking test after the profit action becomes primary. Following that order can switch live bidding to an empty or incorrect profit signal.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The numbered reference promotes the action before it verifies a test order with profit and revenue. The main workflow tells the agent to follow that reference step by step.

content.user_title: Set Up WooCommerce Profit Bidding in Google Ads
content.value_statement: A campaign can meet its revenue target and still lose money after product costs, payment fees, and shipping. Use Product Metrics to verify profit tracking and plan a campaign switch to bidding on profit.
actual_capabilities: Check setup status through the Product Metrics CLI or MCP when authorized access is available.
Guide WooCommerce plugin setup, linking to the Google Ads client account, and Merchant Center prerequisites.
Explain how WooCommerce cost fields and Product Metrics additional costs affect the reported profit value.
Help verify paid test order delivery and distinguish the Profit and Revenue conversion actions.
Use available campaign POAS reporting to suggest a starting target and verify conversion action status after a manual switch.
limitations: Live setup requires Product Metrics Pro, the WooCommerce plugin, and access to the Google Ads client account and its linked Merchant Center.
You must authorize account connections and make primary conversion and bid strategy changes yourself in Google Ads.
Profit tracking requires visitor consent for analytics and ad user data. Orders with unresolved costs do not receive a profit value.
This skill does not configure new customer, returning customer, or lifetime value bidding.

use_cases.title: Check Profit Tracking Readiness
use_cases.description: Find out whether your store connection, consent banner, and cost sources are ready for a paid test order.

use_cases.title: Plan a Single-Campaign Switch
use_cases.description: Use observed campaign POAS to propose a starting target and identify the Google Ads settings you will change.

use_cases.title: Investigate Missing Profit Values
use_cases.description: Trace missing values to product costs, payment fees, shipping costs, or consent before putting profit values into bidding.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Profit Bidding
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Learn which conversion value to use.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the difference between revenue bidding and profit bidding for my WooCommerce store. List the prerequisites without accessing any accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Setup: Identify what is missing before running a test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the setup status for my confirmed Product Metrics workspace and property. Tell me what remains before a paid test order. Do not change settings or retrieve individual orders.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Missing Profit
prompt_templates.scenario: Troubleshooting: A test order has revenue but no profit.
prompt_templates.prompt: My paid test order shows revenue but no profit. Use my redacted cost and consent settings to identify what to check. Do not request customer details or credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Profit Bidding Pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Prepare a switch for one campaign.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my verified campaign-level POAS to suggest a starting target ROAS for one campaign. List the Google Ads changes I must make and the checks to run afterward. Do not apply changes.

output_examples.input: Our paid test order shows revenue, but the profit column is empty.
output: Check that WooCommerce uses the correct product cost source and that additional costs are active.
If a required cost is unknown, the order can be sent with revenue only.
Keep the profit action secondary until a paid test order shows the expected profit value.

output_examples.input: One campaign has a verified POAS of 1.5. What target should we try?
output: Start with a 150% target ROAS on the profit conversion value, rather than reusing the revenue target.
Test one campaign using Maximize conversion value. Review its results after a few weeks before changing other campaigns.

best_practices: Confirm the Google Ads client account, verify consent, and check the expected profit on a paid test order before enabling profit bidding.
Keep one purchase action primary for the intended bidding scope and retain the old action as secondary for comparison.
Use one campaign as a pilot and base its starting target on verified campaign POAS.
anti_patterns: Reusing a revenue-based target ROAS unchanged after switching the conversion value to profit.
Making both the revenue and profit purchase actions primary for the same bidding scope.
Sharing a WooCommerce setup token or customer order details in chat.

faq.question: What does POAS mean?
faq.answer: POAS means profit on ad spend. It compares the profit value sent to Google Ads with the cost of advertising.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics Pro and Merchant Center?
faq.answer: Yes. This workflow uses Product Metrics Pro and requires a Merchant Center account linked to your Google Ads client account.

faq.question: What happens when a product cost is missing?
faq.answer: Product Metrics can fall back to a matching Merchant Center cost or a configured percentage. If a required cost remains unknown, it sends revenue only.

faq.question: How are losses and refunds handled?
faq.answer: Loss-making orders send a profit value of zero. Product Metrics adjusts the Google Ads conversion when WooCommerce reports a refund.

faq.question: Can the assistant make my profit conversion primary?
faq.answer: No. You make that change in Google Ads. The assistant can verify the conversion action status afterward with authorized access.

faq.question: Can I still bid on revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Product Metrics - Revenue instead of Product Metrics - Profit as the primary purchase action for that bidding scope.
